name: Hyderabad
tagline: Nizam splendour, biryani and a thriving tech metropolis.
bestMonths: Jan, Feb, Oct, Nov and Dec
whenBlurb: October to February is the pleasant window, from Bathukamma's flowers to winter's Numaish fair; avoid the parched April-to-June heat.

ourTake.lede: Hyderabad is a Nizam city that few outsiders read properly, it's biryani, pearls and Qutb Shahi grandeur, not an IT park. See the Charminar and the old city early, then give real time to the Golconda Fort at sunset for the light and the sound-and-light show. Skip the mall version of Hyderabadi food and eat the real biryani where the old families do; the Chowmahalla Palace is the underrated star.
ourTake.comeIf: You want Nizami grandeur, the biryani of record and a landmark palace hotel.
ourTake.skipIf: You want a beach, hills or a marquee holiday destination.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Taj Falaknuma Palace
credentials: Three MICHELIN Keys (2025), the highest distinction, shared in India only with Taj Lake Palace, Udaipur
Travel + Leisure India, Best Heritage Hotel
Condé Nast Traveller UK, Gold List / world's best hotels (readers)
items.description: The Nizam's own palace on a hilltop above the old city, one of the greatest hotels in India, and it feels it.

items.name: ITC Kohenur, a Luxury Collection Hotel
credentials: Marriott Luxury Collection
LEED Platinum, LEED Zero Carbon & LEED Zero Water certified (sustainability firsts)
Home to Dum Pukht Begum's, ITC's flagship Nizami-Awadhi table
items.description: A Luxury Collection tower named for the Koh-i-Noor, overlooking the lake in the new-city business heart.

items.name: Park Hyatt Hyderabad
credentials: MICHELIN Guide hotel
Park Hyatt, Hyatt's luxury flagship brand
items.description: Contemporary Hyatt luxury in the city's most distinguished neighbourhood, calm, design-led, quietly grand.

items.name: Taj Krishna
credentials: Taj Hotels, maison group
The Chambers members' club & Encounters bar (long-standing city landmark)
items.description: The Taj's grande-dame in Banjara Hills, thirteen acres of green in the heart of the old-money city.

items.name: Trident Hyderabad
credentials: Trident, an Oberoi Group brand
Consistently top-ranked Hyderabad hotel (Tripadvisor readers)
items.description: The Oberoi group's polished HITEC City house, understated, faultlessly run, in the tech heart.

items.name: Novotel Hyderabad Convention Centre
credentials: Accor, Novotel brand
Adjoining HICC, India's largest purpose-built convention centre
items.description: Fifteen garden acres beside India's largest convention centre, the natural base for a large gathering.

items.name: The Charminar
credentials: On the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List as part of the Qutb Shahi Monuments of Hyderabad
items.description: The 1591 four-minaret gateway is the soul of the old city, its granite arches rising over the chaos of the bazaars around it. Climb the narrow spiral stair at golden hour, then let a private guide thread you through the lanes below.

items.name: Laad Bazaar (the bangle market)
items.description: The lane radiating from the Charminar is a river of lacquer bangles, pearls and bridal finery, unchanged in trade for four centuries. A trusted dealer will bring the good pearls out from the back, away from the crush.

items.name: Mecca Masjid
items.description: One of India's largest and oldest mosques, its central arches raised from bricks said to be brought from Mecca, holding ten thousand worshippers beside the Charminar. Dress modestly; the courtyard is best in the quiet before Friday prayers.

items.name: Golconda Fort
credentials: On the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List as part of the Qutb Shahi Monuments of Hyderabad
items.description: The Qutb Shahi citadel climbs a granite hill in concentric ramparts, and its famous acoustics carry a hand-clap at the entrance clear to the pavilion on top. A dawn climb before the heat, with a guide who knows the water system and the secret passages, is the way to do it.

items.name: Golconda sound-and-light show
items.description: After dark the ramparts light in sequence while a narrated history of the fort and the Koh-i-Noor plays across the stone, English on set evenings. Book the English show ahead and carry a wrap; the hilltop cools fast.

items.name: Qutb Shahi Tombs
credentials: On the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List as part of the Qutb Shahi Monuments of Hyderabad
items.description: The necropolis of the sultans, thirty domed tombs and a mortuary bath in a garden below the fort, has been meticulously restored over the past decade and reopened as a heritage park. It is quieter and more moving than the fort; go with someone who can read the calligraphy.

items.name: Chowmahalla Palace
items.description: The Nizams' ceremonial seat, four palaces around courtyards and a Belgian-crystal Durbar Hall, with the vintage-car collection and a 1930s Rolls in the forecourt. It is the clearest window onto Asaf Jahi grandeur; take the guided route to catch the details.

items.name: Taj Falaknuma Palace, high tea and heritage walk
items.description: The Nizam's cloud-palace, 2,000 feet above the city, is now a Taj hotel, and the afternoon heritage walk with an art historian ends in high tea served on the Jade Terrace or in the Gol Bungalow. This is the single most Nizami afternoon in Hyderabad; the day tour is booked in advance and usually runs weekends.

items.name: A night at Taj Falaknuma Palace
items.description: To actually stay is to dine at the world's longest banquet table, be received at the porte-cochere with rose petals, and walk the Jade Room and library after the day guests have gone. For a multi-generational trip it is the anchor experience; suites go quickly.

items.name: Salar Jung Museum
items.description: The world's largest one-man collection, some 43,000 objects amassed by Salar Jung III, from the Veiled Rebecca marble to a musical clock that draws a crowd on the hour. Half a day with a curator-led guide barely scratches it; closed Fridays.

items.name: The Nizam's Museum, Purani Haveli
items.description: The sixth Nizam's 176-foot Burmese-teak walk-in wardrobe with its hand-cranked lift, and the silver-jubilee gifts of the last Nizam, fill the old family palace. It is intimate and eccentric where Chowmahalla is grand; a short, rewarding stop.

items.name: Paigah Tombs
items.description: A hidden 18th-century necropolis of the Nizams' nobility, its lime-stucco and pierced marble jaali screens so fine they draw comparison to the Alhambra, now beautifully restored. Few tourists find it; go with a guide who can point out the geometry.

items.name: Taramati Baradari
items.description: A Qutb Shahi pleasure pavilion of arched bays set on a rise near Golconda, tied to the legend of the courtesan whose song carried to the fort. Restored as a cultural venue, it is a serene stop and a fine sunset perch.

items.name: Hussain Sagar and the Buddha statue
items.description: The heart-shaped lake dug in 1563 holds a single 58-foot monolithic Buddha on a mid-water rock, reached by a short boat ride. A dusk cruise from Lumbini Park, city lights coming up around the water, is the classic pause.

items.name: Necklace Road
items.description: The lamp-lit promenade curving along the lake takes its name from the way it strings the shore like a necklace of lights. It is where the city walks in the evening; good for a slow stroll or a private car cruise before dinner.

items.name: Birla Mandir
items.description: A white-marble Vishnu temple on a granite hill, carved in Rajasthani and Dravidian styles, glowing at dusk above the lake. The climb rewards you with the best free panorama of the twin cities; leave footwear and cameras at the base.

items.name: B. M. Birla Science Museum and Planetarium
items.description: Below the temple, the planetarium's dome-projected sky shows and the science galleries with a dinosaur skeleton are a genuine hit with children. A good hour for a multi-generational group needing a change of pace from monuments.

items.name: Shilparamam crafts village
items.description: An arts-and-crafts village where weavers, bidri-workers and dyers sell direct, with a rolling rural bazaar and folk performances at the amphitheatre. It is the easiest place to meet artisans and buy well without haggling in the old-city crush.

items.name: Durgam Cheruvu and the cable bridge
credentials: Longest precast-segmental concrete extradosed cable-stayed span in the world
items.description: A rock-fringed lake once hidden inside the tech corridor, now crossed by a floodlit extradosed cable bridge that changes colour at night. It is the modern face of the city; walk the lakeside boardwalk after dark for the light show on the water.

items.name: KBR National Park
items.description: A pocket of Deccan scrub forest in the smartest part of town, its shaded loop a favourite morning walk for peacocks, wildflowers and the city's power-walkers. A calm green start to a day; go at opening for the birds.

items.name: Nehru Zoological Park
items.description: One of India's larger zoos, with a lion-and-tiger safari drive-through and a nocturnal-animals house, set in green near the old city. An easy multi-generational morning; the safari bus is the draw for children.

items.name: The Hyderabadi biryani pilgrimage
items.description: The dum biryani, rice and meat sealed and slow-cooked, served with mirchi-ka-salan and dahi chutney, is the city's edible crown, and every family swears by a different house. A private food guide can run a tasting across the legends, with the vegetable and kachche-gosht versions side by side.

items.name: The Irani café ritual, Irani chai and Osmania biscuits
items.description: The Persian-origin cafés of Hyderabad pour strong sweet Irani chai alongside the crumbly, faintly savoury Osmania biscuit, a century-old morning rite. Ten minutes at a marble-topped table tells you more about the city than an hour in a museum.

items.name: Haleem in the old city (seasonal)
credentials: Hyderabadi Haleem holds a Geographical Indication (GI) tag
items.description: During Ramzan the lanes fill with the slow-pounded wheat-and-meat haleem, a Hyderabadi speciality with its own protected geographical status, cooked overnight in vast cauldrons. If your trip lands in the holy month, an evening haleem crawl is unmissable.

items.name: Vegetarian Hyderabadi and Andhra thali
items.description: Amid the famous meat there is a deep vegetarian table too, bagara baingan, the tamarind-and-lentil pappu, and the fiery banana-leaf Andhra meals of the tech-city restaurants. Worth booking for travellers who don't eat meat but still want the regional flavour.

items.name: Pearl shopping (the City of Pearls)
items.description: Hyderabad has been India's pearl-drilling and trading capital for centuries, and the old houses around the Charminar still sort, drill and string by hand. Buy from an established, certified house; a knowledgeable guide keeps you clear of the imitations.

items.name: Bidri craft and Nizami metalwork
credentials: Bidriware carries a Geographical Indication (GI) tag
items.description: Bidriware, black zinc alloy inlaid with silver in floral Persian motifs, is a Deccan art with its own GI tag, and Hyderabad is a prime place to buy the finest pieces. A vase or a paandan makes the most characterful souvenir of the region.

items.name: Sunday Chor Bazaar
items.description: The centuries-old flea market spreads on Sundays into a maze of colonial-era brass, old cameras, vinyl and Nizam-era curios. A treasure hunt for collectors; go early with a local who can spot the real from the reproduced.

items.name: Moazzam Jahi Market
items.description: A restored 1930s Osmanian-Gothic market building, its clock tower now floodlit, famous for its old-school fruit ice-creams and the buzz of the surrounding lanes. A characterful evening stop between the old and new cities.

items.name: Chowmahalla to Charminar heritage walk
items.description: A guided morning on foot through the old-city lanes ties the palace, the mosque, the Charminar and the bazaars into a single narrative of the Qutb Shahi and Asaf Jahi city. The best single way to grasp how the old Hyderabad fits together; go early to beat the heat.

items.name: State Gallery of Art
items.description: Telangana's flagship public art museum holds a broad collection of modern and contemporary Indian work in a purpose-built gallery near the tech corridor. A cool, uncrowded hour for those who want art beyond the antiquities.

items.name: Sudha Cars Museum
items.description: A gloriously eccentric private collection of hand-built working cars shaped like a shoe, a cricket bat, a burger and more, the largest such museum of its kind. Odd, joyful and a sure hit with children.

items.name: Lumbini Park and the lake laser show
items.description: The lakeside park is the jetty for the Buddha-statue boats and stages an evening musical laser-fountain show on the water. A gentle sunset add-on to a lake cruise, easy with young family.

items.name: Spanish Mosque (Aiwan-e-Begumpet)
items.description: A rare Moorish-revival mosque with octagonal spires modelled on Andalusian Spain, built by a Paigah noble and unlike anything else in India. A quiet architectural curiosity a short drive from the airport road.

items.name: Toli Masjid and the Qutb Shahi road to Golconda
items.description: A 1671 mosque of exquisite stucco arches on the historic road between the city and Golconda, often missed on the standard circuit. For those who have done the headline monuments and want the connoisseur's stop.

items.name: Ramoji Film City (day trip)
credentials: Guinness World Record, largest film studio complex in the world
items.description: The Guinness-certified largest film studio complex in the world, 2,000 acres of permanent sets, gardens and shows that double as a theme park. A full day, best with a premium guided package and a golf-cart tour; superb for multi-generational groups.

items.name: Warangal Fort (day trip)
items.description: The 13th-century Kakatiya capital survives in the four monumental Kala Thoranam stone gateways and the ruined Swayambhu temple, emblem of Telangana itself. Pair it with the Ramappa and Thousand-Pillar temples for a rich day of Kakatiya history.

items.name: Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) Temple (day trip)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed 2021, the only World Heritage Site in Telangana
items.description: The 1213 Shiva temple famed for its 'floating' porous bricks and its bracket-figures of dancers is Telangana's first UNESCO World Heritage Site. A longer excursion, ideally combined with an overnight near Warangal; the carving rewards a slow, guided look.

items.name: Thousand Pillar Temple, Hanamkonda (day trip)
items.description: A star-shaped 12th-century Kakatiya temple to Shiva, Vishnu and Surya, its monolithic Nandi and finely lathe-turned pillars a masterclass in Deccan stone craft. A natural companion to Warangal Fort on the same day.

items.name: Bhongir (Bhuvanagiri) Fort (day trip)
items.description: A single colossal egg-shaped granite monolith crowned by a Kakatiya-era fort, with a stiff stepped climb to sweeping Deccan views. Close enough for a half-day; now also a spot for rock-climbing and rappelling.

items.name: Nagarjuna Sagar and Nagarjunakonda island (day trip)
items.description: One of the world's tallest masonry dams, and a mid-reservoir island reached only by ferry that holds a museum of relocated 2nd-century Buddhist ruins from the drowned valley of Vijayapuri. A full day; the boat runs to a fixed morning schedule, closed Fridays.

items.name: Ananthagiri Hills, Vikarabad (day trip)
items.description: Cool, forested Deccan hills with an ancient Anantha Padmanabha Swamy temple, the source-streams of the Musi river and easy walking trails. A green-lung escape for a half or full day when the city heat presses.

items.name: Medak Cathedral (day trip)
items.description: A soaring 1924 Gothic-revival church of the Church of South India, seating five thousand under stained glass and reputed to be one of Asia's largest cathedrals. A striking, uncrowded excursion, good paired with the nearby Medak Fort.

items.name: Pocharam and Ananthagiri wildlife (birding day trip)
items.description: The Pocharam lake and sanctuary and the Ananthagiri forests draw migratory waterfowl and Deccan woodland birds within a couple of hours of the city. For naturalists wanting a quiet, guided morning away from the monument trail.

items.name: Yadadri (Yadagirigutta) temple (day trip)
items.description: A hilltop Narasimha temple recently rebuilt on a monumental scale in black granite, now one of Telangana's grandest pilgrimage sites. A striking half-day for those drawn to living temple architecture; combine with Bhongir Fort.

items.name: Adaa
credentials: Inside Taj Falaknuma Palace, Three MICHELIN Keys (2025)
Recognised in India's top-restaurant listings (Condé Nast Traveller / Elite Traveller features)
items.description: Royal Hyderabadi cooking on the palace terrace, the Nizam's city glittering below, the grandest table in Hyderabad.

items.name: Dum Pukht Begum's
credentials: Inside ITC Kohenur, a Luxury Collection Hotel
ITC's celebrated Dum Pukht dining brand
items.description: ITC's flagship Nizami-Awadhi table, biryani and nehari sealed and slow-cooked over a low flame, exactly as it should be.

items.name: Chutneys
credentials: Times Food & Nightlife Awards Hyderabad, Best Vegetarian Restaurant / Most Authentic South Indian (2023 & 2024)
items.description: Hyderabad's most-loved vegetarian house, South Indian tiffin and thalis done with real pride.

items.name: Manam Chocolate Karkhana
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller India x Zomato Top Restaurant Awards 2024, Hyderabad's sole entry
items.description: India's most talked-about chocolate, bean-to-bar from Indian cacao, in a café that has put Hyderabad on the national food map.

items.name: Ohri's
credentials: Home-grown Hyderabad dining group since 1976, 28 brands across the city
Times Food & Nightlife Awards Hyderabad, recognised restaurateur
items.description: Hyderabad's home-grown dining group since 1976, from the cavernous Gufaa to grand banquet halls, a city institution.

items.name: Paradise
credentials: A legend since 1953, the city's oldest and best-known biryani institution
Limca Book of Records, most biryanis served in a year
items.description: The name Hyderabad gave the world for biryani, a legend since 1953, and still the first plate visitors are told to eat.

items.name: Shah Ghouse
credentials: Featured by The Wall Street Journal among India's best biryani
Long-standing city institution (since the 1980s)
items.description: The biryani (and Ramzan haleem) Hyderabadis choose to impress a visitor, heavier on ghee, closer to the old Nizami style.

items.name: Hotel Shadab
credentials: Long-standing Old City institution near Charminar (decades of continuous repute)
items.description: The Old City institution by the Charminar, biryani, kebabs and Ramzan haleem in the thick of old Hyderabad.

items.name: Bawarchi
credentials: Long-standing single-outlet biryani institution (RTC X Roads), no branches, by repute
items.description: A decades-old single-location legend, for many locals, simply the best mutton biryani in the city.

items.name: Gol Bungalow / palace terraces, Taj Falaknuma Palace
credentials: Inside Taj Falaknuma Palace, Three MICHELIN Keys (2025)
items.description: A drink on the Nizam's own palace terrace, the city's lights spread below, the grandest evening in Hyderabad.

items.name: Encounters, Taj Krishna
credentials: Inside Taj Krishna, Taj Hotels
items.description: A long-standing Banjara Hills hotel bar, clubby, discreet, part of the city's social furniture for decades.

items.name: The Living Room, Park Hyatt Hyderabad
credentials: Inside Park Hyatt Hyderabad, MICHELIN Guide hotel
items.description: A serene, design-led lounge in the city's best-run luxury hotel, considered cocktails, quiet and adult.

plan.heading: 3 days in Hyderabad, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Begin at Golconda fort in the morning cool, then the Qutb Shahi tombs alongside.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Chowmahalla Palace and the Nizam jewels, then the lanes of Laad Bazaar for bangles and pearls.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Adaa in the Taj Falaknuma Palace, Nizami cuisine under chandeliers.

days.label: Day 2
days.title: Old city and the Salar Jung

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Charminar and the Mecca Masjid at first light, before the market fills.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Salar Jung Museum, one of the finest single-collector holdings in the country.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Haleem and biryani done properly at Shah Ghouse or Bawarchi, in season.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A slow morning at the Chowmahalla or the Paigah tombs, quieter and exquisitely stuccoed.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Tea by Hussain Sagar or a drive to the Deccan rock formations at the city's edge.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A final dinner at Falaknuma's Celeste terrace before departure.

items.name: Banjara Hills / Jubilee Hills
items.description: The upmarket district with the best hotels and restaurants, the comfortable base.

items.name: Old City (Charminar)
items.description: The Qutb Shahi heart of bazaars and monuments, intense and historic by day.

items.name: Hitec City / Gachibowli
items.description: The modern tech quarter, convenient for business, less for sightseeing.

events.name: Bonalu
events.note: A vibrant folk festival honouring the goddess Mahakali across the twin cities' temples.

events.name: Bathukamma
events.note: Telangana's flower festival, when women build and float towering floral arrangements.

events.name: Ramzan / Haleem season
events.note: The old city comes alive at night for iftar and the famous slow-cooked haleem; dates shift yearly.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Stay in Banjara Hills or Jubilee Hills for calm and the best tables; the Charminar and Chowmahalla areas reward an early-morning visit before the heat and crowds, and Hyderabadi biryani and haleem are worth planning a meal around.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Rajiv Gandhi international airport and take a private chauffeur into the city; the airport is well south of the centre, so allow forty-five minutes to an hour to reach Banjara Hills or the old city.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private car and driver is the practical choice given the distances and traffic; the metro is efficient but rarely relevant for a discerning visitor.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Excellent 4G and 5G across the city on all networks; eSIMs and hotel wifi are seamless.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Indian rupee; cards and UPI are near-universal, but keep a little cash for the old-city bazaars; ten percent is a fair restaurant tip.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: November–February is the kind season: dry, warm days and cool evenings on the Deccan plateau. Avoid April–June, when the heat runs 40°C+, and the July–September monsoon if you dislike rain.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Direct from Delhi (~2h15m), Mumbai (~1h30m) and Bengaluru (~1h) into a genuinely excellent airport (RGIA, HYD); Air India flies business on the Delhi/Mumbai trunk routes, IndiGo dominates frequency. Use the airport's premium lounge and the fast, uncongested expressway into the city, one of India's smoothest arrivals.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations beyond routine. A safe, easy metro; normal city common-sense after dark. No altitude. Tap water is not for drinking, sealed bottled water, and be a little careful with street food if your stomach is sensitive.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Superb for vegetarian and among the easier cities for Jain. While Hyderabad is famous for biryani, its vegetarian and South Indian scene is deep, and dedicated Jain/pure-veg kitchens are common. Chutneys (the restaurant), Rayalaseema Ruchulu for veg thalis, and the Jain-friendly kitchens at the Taj Falaknuma Palace and ITC Kohenur are all reliably good.
